problem: Existing semantic navigation benchmarks are indoor-focused and do not capture outdoor last-mile delivery in residential areas or long-term sequential operation. Prior navigation approaches either need high-precision pre-built maps or are learning-based methods (ViNT/NoMaD) that generalize poorly and need pre-collected data.
motivation: Last-mile delivery robots need to be easy to deploy at scale without labor-intensive pre-mapping, and to understand free-form delivery instructions. Public OpenStreetMap offers a lightweight map, while LLMs/VLMs provide instruction understanding and open-vocabulary perception that can complement classic localization and planning.
key_idea: Combine OpenStreetMap as a lightweight map with LLM task planning, VLM (MobileSAM+CLIP) global localization, map update and house-number recognition, and classical planners, plus a new Gazebo last-mile delivery benchmark with long-term metrics (LSR, LSPL).
insight: Using OSM as the map plus foundation-model modules and classic planners gives far better success than learning-based topological-graph methods (ViNT/NoMaD) in outdoor delivery, with maps about 0.01% of the topological map size. The map-update ablation shows that writing detected house numbers back into OSM raises SPL on all three test destinations (e.g. 34.72% to 51.34%). The LLM comparison shows task-planning reliability varies greatly between models (0.27 to 1.0 SRTP).
method: LLM-based task planning: prompts convert multilingual free-form instructions into hierarchical addresses (with a verification prompt), optimize task order/grouping, and query OSM from lowest to highest sub-address to generate the task sequence
Navigation mode: OSM road network converted to a hierarchical graph and routed with Multi-Level Dijkstra to give global waypoints

Exploration mode: when OSM lacks entrance details, compute the building's concave hull, inflate it, uniformly sample waypoints facing the centroid, and use a VLM on RGB images to recognize the target house number
VLM global localization: MobileSAM segments the image, CLIP labels segments against OSM element types, labeled points are projected to a BEV and registered 2D with OSM geometry to give a global pose
Map update: newly detected elements such as house number plates are added into OSM to speed up later deliveries
Local localization and planning: FastLIO2 for local pose, factor graph fusing global localization as prior factors, A* on an OSM-derived costmap and Timed Elastic Band for trajectories
Benchmark metrics: SRTP, SR, SPL, plus Long-term SR (LSR) and LSPL with exponential-decay task weights (r=0.9)

setting.backbone: GPT-4o-mini etc. LLM for planning, VLM for house-number recognition, MobileSAM + CLIP (frozen) plus classical FastLIO2/A*/TEB
setting.observation: monocular RGB camera + Livox MID-360 LiDAR (+GPS in real world for evaluation only)
setting.action_space: waypoints executed by classical planner (A* + Timed Elastic Band), differential-drive velocity control
setting.simulator: Gazebo (three custom worlds: small, medium, large) plus real-world campus
setting.privileged: OSM map of the environment (not GT pose); house-number detection via VLM

numbers.eval_set_note: 5 individual tasks for SR/SPL; 5 continuous deliveries for LSR/LSPL

numbers_note: Very small evaluation (5 tasks per world). Real-world results only qualitative (human operator SPL 96.1%; OPEN SPL not explicitly given). SRTP by LLM: Gemini-1.5-pro 0.27, Qwen-turbo 0.5, WenXinYiYan 0.6, GPT-3.5-turbo 0.9, Claude-3.5 0.97, GPT-4o-mini 1.0 (60 runs each).
results: On the new Gazebo benchmark OPEN reaches 100% SR in small and medium and 60% in large worlds, while ViNT/NoMaD get 40%/20%/0% (SPL at most 21.13%/18.23%/0). In the real-world campus test OPEN completed the two-building delivery while ViNT and NoMaD collided and failed.
limitations: Tiny evaluation (5 tasks per world, one real-world two-delivery run), and only ViNT/NoMaD as baselines
SPL is modest even when SR is 100%, and sequential execution reduces success (3 of 5 tasks in medium/large)
Depends on OSM availability/quality and LLM choice (SRTP varies widely across LLMs); simulation worlds are synthetic
